Topics

What we'll cover

Sessions follow your exam board's specification and your target grade. These are the main areas.

Pure Mathematics

  • Algebra and functions
  • Coordinate geometry
  • Sequences and series
  • Trigonometry
  • Exponentials and logarithms
  • Differentiation and integration
  • Proof, vectors and numerical methods

Statistics

  • Sampling and data presentation, including the large data set
  • Probability
  • Binomial and normal distributions
  • Hypothesis testing

Mechanics

  • Kinematics, including variable acceleration
  • Forces and Newton's laws
  • Moments
  • Projectiles
The exams

How the exams work

A-level Maths is examined in three 2-hour papers, each worth 100 marks. How Pure, Statistics and Mechanics are split between the papers depends on the exam board, so we work from your board's specification and past papers.

Exam technique

Where marks are usually lost

  • Algebraic slips in long, multi-step questions
  • Not showing enough working in “show that” and proof questions
  • Mechanics modelling: naming the assumptions the question is looking for
  • Hypothesis test conclusions that aren't written in context

FAQ

A-level Maths: common questions

Which exam boards do you teach?

AQA, Edexcel and OCR. Sessions are tailored to the board your school sits, so the question styles match your papers.

Can sessions focus on the topics I find hardest?

That's what the free intro call is for: we talk through what's needed (topics, exam board and target grade) and plan from there.

Do you teach Year 12 and Year 13?

Yes, both years of the A-level, tailored to what the student is covering in school.
